status: prospective protocol; not executed; no results claimed
question: When medication sources change, do stored derivations improve repeated evidence retrieval enough to justify their construction and maintenance cost, and are all candidate judgments kept correct?
design: 2 x 2 comparison: Neo4j and file-backed SQLite, each with query-time derivation and stored derivation
primary_application: Which medication-tariff candidates and route judgments changed after a source refresh, what source records caused the changes, and which linked records require follow-up?

sources.initial: included June medication extracts and frozen tariff catalogue
sources.refresh: first eligible later complete official release acquired after this protocol is fixed
sources.eligibility: complete documented SAI/Refdata and SL publications; unchanged tariff version for the primary source-refresh contrast
sources.freeze_before_execution: source hashes, acquisition date, parsing rules, workloads and tuning choices
sources.fallback: the included earlier-to-June transition may be used as development data only; it is not the independent evaluation population

arms: Neo4j stored witness-to-tariff relationship retaining every derivation and premise
SQLite indexed stored witness-to-tariff table retaining every derivation and premise
fairness: Identical source records, interpretation rules, complete outputs and multiplicities in all arms
Every stored graph relationship has an equivalent relational table row
Same host, HTTP transport, response fields and complete row consumption
Document memory, storage, indexes, query plans and software versions
Tune on development data before the independent release is acquired; record revisions transparently
Use a dedicated disposable database; retain raw source snapshots
workloads: All five existing source-explanation tasks with unchanged output contracts
Candidate and judgment changes between the two source releases
Affected source premises and candidate explanations after refresh

measurements.correctness: complete pair, derivation, premise and judgment equality against independent source reconstruction before and after every update
measurements.latency: median and quartiles of full-output retrieval; paired observed differences
measurements.materialization: initial construction time, relationship or row counts and extra storage
measurements.refresh: refresh time and invalidation count; stale candidate and stale judgment counts must be zero
measurements.total_cost: construction plus refresh plus repeated retrieval at 1, 10, 100 and 1000 requests; report observed break-even only when it exists
measurements.protocol: three warmups and fifteen randomized interleaved retrieval repetitions; seven independent construction/refresh cycles from an identical starting state
measurements.uncertainty: report timing distributions and dependent units; repeat counts are not independent medication observations

acceptance: Every arm matches independently reconstructed source-derived answers
Every refreshed answer exposes its exact source changes
No elapsed-time advantage is inferred from query brevity or join count
Report unfavorable, tied and favorable outcomes symmetrically
An engineering benefit is claimed only for its measured arm, workload and refresh frequency
interpretation_limits: This experiment measures deployment choices and update correctness. It does not measure human comprehension, acquisition effort, clinical outcomes or reimbursement entitlement. A real evidence-acquisition study would additionally need unknown fields from a heterogeneous new cohort and independently documented retrieval effort.
